subject: Accountancy
chapter: Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm – Admission of a Partner
central_question: How are profit-sharing rights, goodwill, reserves, asset values and capitals adjusted fairly when a new partner is admitted or the existing partners change their ratio?
in_scope_units: Modes of reconstitution and the meaning, rights and consent requirements of admission.
Calculation of the new profit-sharing ratio and the sacrificing ratio.
Meaning, factors, need and methods of valuation of goodwill.
Treatment of goodwill when premium is brought fully, partly or not at all and when goodwill already appears in the books.
Accounting Standard 26 implications and calculation of hidden goodwill.
Adjustment of accumulated profits, losses and reserves in the old ratio.
Revaluation of assets, reassessment of liabilities and treatment of unrecorded items.
Adjustment of partners’ capitals in the new ratio.
Change in profit-sharing ratio among existing partners, including gaining and sacrificing adjustments.
banned_topics: Settlement of a retiring or deceased partner, which belongs to the next reconstitution chapter.
Realisation Account and closure of the firm, which belong to dissolution.
Company goodwill arising from business combinations beyond the partnership treatment in this chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Admission dissolves and closes the partnership firm.
known_pitfalls.correction: Admission reconstitutes the partnership agreement; the firm continues with a changed composition and a new agreement.

known_pitfalls.claim: The incoming partner’s goodwill premium is credited to all partners in the new ratio.
known_pitfalls.correction: It compensates the old partners who sacrifice profit share and is credited to them in the sacrificing ratio.

known_pitfalls.claim: Revaluation profit belongs to all partners including the incoming partner.
known_pitfalls.correction: It arose before admission and is transferred only to old partners in their old profit-sharing ratio.

known_pitfalls.claim: Internally generated goodwill should remain as an asset after reconstitution.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter’s AS 26 discussion states that internally generated goodwill is not recognised; book goodwill is written off at reconstitution.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Illustrations 1–5 to calculate new profit-sharing ratios under different acquisition terms.
Use NCERT Illustrations 6–8 to calculate sacrifice or gain from old and new shares.
Use NCERT Illustrations 9–15 to value goodwill by average profit, super profit and capitalisation methods.
Use NCERT Illustrations 16–21 to record premium, book goodwill, goodwill not brought and hidden goodwill.
Use NCERT Illustrations 22–24 to adjust reserves and prepare the Revaluation Account.
Use NCERT Illustrations 25–27 to align capital balances with the new ratio and prepare the reconstituted balance sheet.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Questions for Practice containing Short Answer, Long Answer and Numerical Questions on admission, ratios, goodwill, revaluation, reserves and capital adjustment.
